speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You have presented with progressive swelling and pain in your right ring finger. To begin, has this pain been present continuously, or does it come and go in episodes?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: That mechanism of injury suggests trauma, but the persistence of swelling and pain raises concern for infection. Did you notice any redness, warmth, or drainage from the finger, or did you have any fever after the injury?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Trigger Finger (Stenosing Tenosynovitis) of the right ring finger, likely chronic inflammation or post-traumatic stenosis causing mechanical locking at the A1 pulley.

I am Dr. Agent. You describe a classic "locking" mechanism where your finger is stuck in extension and you cannot flex it at the distal joint. Given the inability to make a fist and the specific extension at rest, we need to confirm inflammation of the flexor tendon. REQUEST TEST: Ultrasound of the right ring finger flexor tendons to check for tendon thickening and tenosynovitis.

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
